notes: Summary: Enterprise-regulated customer evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for regulated document search + support assistant for EU customers.
Initial value: replace current on-prem LLM stack to reduce ops cost while keeping residency + control.
Call 2026-02-18 (intro) — attendees: Maya (AE), Lucas (SE), CTO (Hightower), Head of InfoSec. CTO: "Need airtight data residency + key control."
Security workshop 2026-03-02 — requested: full SIG/CAIQ, CAIQ evidence artifacts, network topology for VPC peering, flow for logs (retention 7 years), and KMS BYOK options.
Procurement asked for vendor risk intake form (attached in Drive). Legal flagged: liability language around model outputs + deletion after retention window.

POC ask: 30-day pilot in customer-managed VPC, peered to Hightower AWS account, provisioned via Terraform module. Goal metrics: chat p95 < 120ms, 99th token latency SLA for short prompts, baseline throughput 350-500 rps for embeddings batch jobs overnight.

KMS notes: customer uses AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys; wants envelope encryption and key rotation visibility. SE: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (Azure/AWS) via key-wrapping; need architecture diagram and proof-of-concept doc.
Audit logging: retention policy strict (7 years), immutable logs, push to customer SIEM (Splunk). Need confirmation of log delivery (push vs pull) and evidence for audit trail integrity.

Shared responsibility: Hightower wants explicit split: Redwood manages runtime/patching of model infra; Hightower retains custody of keys and log archives. Legal wants contractual SLA for data deletion + certification mapping.
Quote from InfoSec: "We will only sign if SIG/CAIQ + artifact pack checks out and we can validate KMS HSM custody."
